links.targetTitle: Collateral qualifies as peg-stabilizing by the price it comm

title: Peg defense may be funded by generating new USDS and borrowing against it to buy USDS back
content:
A.3.3.2.4.2.1 lists two ways to meet a Peg Defense obligation: "(1) selling other types of collateral for USDS, or (2) by using USDS, or generating new USDS via the Allocation System, that is then used as collateral to borrow other types of assets (e.g. USDC or USDT on Aave) and buy USDS with it."

The first is straightforward reserve deployment. The second is worth stating plainly: during an event where USDS is trading below par, an Agent may **issue additional USDS**, pledge it as collateral, borrow dollars against it, and spend those dollars buying USDS.

The accounting works — USDS bought is retired against USDS issued, and the net effect is an increase in the Agent's borrowing against Sky's balance sheet in exchange for removing supply from the market. In normal conditions it is an efficient way to source purchasing power without liquidating productive positions.

The reflexivity is what deserves recording. The route depends on third-party lending markets accepting USDS as collateral at close to par at the exact moment the market is repricing USDS below par. If a discount deepens, those markets will reduce USDS collateral factors or halt borrowing against it — withdrawing the funding channel precisely when the obligation is largest. The mechanism is strongest when it is least needed.

It also means an Agent's *reported* peg defense capacity is not the same as its unencumbered reserve. Two Agents holding identical ASC have very different real firepower depending on how much of their defense would have to be funded through this route, and the framework does not distinguish them: the 6.25%-per-six-hours obligation is measured against the ASC requirement, not against the resources actually available to meet it.
description: A.3.3.2.4.2.1 permits satisfying the obligation by minting USDS via the Allocation System, posting it as collateral to borrow USDC or USDT, and using the proceeds to purchase USDS.
